findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: The only purpose of `profiles.birthday` and `profiles.phone` is the greeting, but the design ties their retention to the profile, not to the opt-in. A member who turns the option off keeps both values in `profiles` for as long as the account lives, with no purpose left (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and (e), Art. 7(3) withdrawal of consent). The spec only covers opting in ("Members opt in to birthday greetings"). Add a requirement and a scenario "WHEN a member opts out THEN their birthday and phone are erased", state in the design that opting out clears both columns, and add the matching task and test.
findings.title: Birthday and phone are kept after the member opts out

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Birth dates and phone numbers are copied into the nightly backups, but nothing says how long those backups are kept, so a value erased on opt-out or account deletion survives there for an undefined time (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17). State the backup retention period in the design (or point to the existing backup policy) and how an erasure reaches restored backups.
findings.title: No retention or purge rule for the copies in nightly backups

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: The processor and the transfer outside the EEA are named, but the plan does not say whether a processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28) and a transfer mechanism (Chapter V: adequacy decision, e.g. the EU-US Data Privacy Framework, or standard contractual clauses) cover Textly, nor whether Textly keeps the numbers and messages it receives, and for how long. Question for the team: record the agreement, the transfer basis and Textly's retention in the design.
findings.title: Transfer of phone numbers and names to Textly in the United States has no stated safeguard

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: The purpose is stated (birthday messages, wanted by marketing), but not the lawful basis (GDPR Art. 6). The opt-in suggests consent; if so, say it in the proposal, together with how consent is recorded and withdrawn. Question for the team: only the controller can tell what was decided.
findings.title: Lawful basis of the processing is not stated
